summary: Retained as a next-day binary prediction task for retrospective research and agent evaluation with the labeled eval split - a demonstrated-headroom finding under the pre-registered rule, not a large-headroom claim. Each row is one CPCB CAAQM PM2.5 station-day D (as republished by the XKDR Forum India Air Quality Database, cpcb_caaqm stream only; us_embassy monitors excluded) at the 23:59 IST prediction instant: predict whether the station's D+1 calendar-day 24-hour mean PM2.5 exceeds 90 ug/m3 (strict >, the Poor-band lower breakpoint of CPCB's own National AQI), with both D and D+1 requiring n_hours >= 18. Features are the station's own daily PM2.5 statistics through day D (mean/max/min, n_hours, lags 1-3, trailing 7/30/90-day means with valid-day counts, days since a >90 day, 30-day exceedance count), the calendar of D and station identity (state_name carrying the declared UNKNOWN_STATE sentinel for the 62 of 549 stations the export leaves null). The label source (next_day_pm25_mean, next_day_n_hours) is excluded from every shipped column; row selection reads day-D completeness plus a D+1 observability rule that never reads the label value, with excluded rows counted per split. The archive is ONE pinned export (exported_at 2026-09-30T11:25:11+00:00, 196,521,834 rows, asserted by the build), so this is retrospective_research with a current_snapshot vintage: no operational as-of claim is made, training-label timing is unverified, and intraday publication latency at CPCB is unmeasured (day-D trailing completeness at the instant is a declared assumption). The measured finding that defines the task, carried beside every figure: on the identical 126,570 eval rows (2023) the stock runner baseline scored eval AUC 0.9734 (both runner implementations agree, on the accepted bytes after re-accept), beating every pre-registered triad member with station-clustered paired bootstrap 95% CIs excluding zero - station_persistence (day-D pm25_mean as the score) 0.9689 (model minus persistence +0.004487, CI [+0.003777, +0.005159], 1,000 resamples, 509 station clusters), state_season_climatology (train rate per state x season of D+1) 0.8617 (+0.111802, CI [+0.100150, +0.125189]), and the degenerate constant global_rate member beaten by the model's own cluster-bootstrap AUC CI [0.971304, 0.975297] lying entirely above 0.5. Persistence itself dominates climatology (+0.107316, CI [+0.095881, +0.120774]) and its supplementary binary >90 rule agrees with the label 93.50% of the time: the label is largely persistence-carried, so the demonstrated model edge over persistence is real but small - that structure is part of the finding and must be stated beside any figure. Majority-class accuracy on eval is 0.8434 (constant fitted on train); global_rate is degenerate as a score (Brier 0.1351). Splits: train 2019-2022 (288,754 rows / 61,075 positives, 21.15%), eval 2023 (126,570 / 19,819, 15.66%, 351 distinct positive days), holdout 2024 (145,124 / 18,222, 12.56%, 352 days, SEALED and never scored). Prevalence declines across the split (21.15% -> 15.66% -> 12.56%): an out-of-distribution as well as temporal test, recorded as a property. Positives are winter-clustered (eval 2023: DJF 33.0% vs JJAS 1.0% prevalence), so distinct-positive-day counts are the conservative independent-observation count and every interval is station-clustered.

cross_row_audit.scope: Row D's label operand (the D+1 24-hr mean) is exactly row D+1's own pm25_mean feature, and the same value enters the trailing aggregates of rows D+2..D+91. The declared probe (quality.json cross_row_audit, next_day_mean_recovery) is the same-station offset-1 blind join: a donor row one day later donates its pm25_mean, and gt 90 reproduces the label BY CONSTRUCTION - a mathematical identity on the shipped columns, not a measured statistical bound (unlike a mismatch-rate probe, no join coverage was measured on this artifact because recovery is exact wherever the join lands). The exposure is real and declared, not argued away. The mitigation is protocol, not absence: access is isolated_rows, the scope is restricted retrospective research, the label source columns (next_day_pm25_mean, next_day_n_hours) are excluded from every shipped file, and honest evaluation keeps rows isolated - consumers must not join across rows.
cross_row_audit.evidence: quality.json cross_row_audit + evaluation_contract.limitations shipped with the artifact (gate-verified bytes, release/cpcb-aqi-exceedance/quality.json sha256 98250e9d...): the probe declaration names the exact recovery identity ('blind-join label recovery: a donor row of the same station one day later donates its pm25_mean, which is exactly this row's label operand; gt 90 reproduces the label by construction'); record.qualification.cross_row_probe_on_real_artifact; gate 1.5.0 passed 45/45 on the full artifact with the contract declared.

supported_uses: Retrospective research and method comparison on the pinned artifact a749f0df, predicting row-wise from the shipped at-instant columns under an isolated-rows protocol, with the labeled eval split (2023) as development/validation

Agent evaluation with the labeled eval split: the consumer is a coding agent that edits the runner's train.py; the recorded comparison (model 0.9734 beside station_persistence 0.9689 and state_season_climatology 0.8617, with the clustered intervals) is the ladder that must be quoted beside any model figure
Reproducibility studies: the export pin (exported_at + row count asserted by the build), digest-pinned artifact, the gate report, references implementation and baseline shipped with the package
unsupported_uses: Operational or live air-quality forecasting claims: the archive is one current-snapshot export with no historical vintages and no first-publication ledger, so no historical point-in-time reconstruction is claimed or evidenced
Any certified historical-forecasting setup: training-label timing is unverified and no full-row availability ledger exists

Reading the model's +0.0045 edge over persistence as large headroom: the label is largely persistence-carried (persistence 0.9689, binary >90 agreement 0.9350) and the edge, while CI-excluding-zero, is small; no model beyond the stock runner has been measured and the holdout is unspent
Quoting any single figure from this dataset without the comparison ladder beside it (model 0.9734 / persistence 0.9689 / climatology 0.8617 on identical eval rows)

Presenting the derived dataset as a CPCB, Government of India, or XKDR Forum product; the sources' designations, requested credits and data-quality caveats ('as reported', 'no gap filling', 'preliminary and not fully validated') carry through unchanged
limitations: The defining measured finding: headroom IS demonstrated under the pre-registered rule (the model beats every triad member with station-clustered CIs excluding zero), but the margin over the strongest member is small - model 0.9734 vs station_persistence 0.9689 (+0.004487, CI [+0.003777, +0.005159]) - and the label is largely persistence-carried; any consumer figure must carry this comparison.

Retrospective closed-export vintage: the build pins ONE XKDR export (exported_at 2026-09-30, 196,521,834 rows) and refuses any other; a second export has never been observed, so revision behaviour is unmeasured and values corrected after publication cannot be distinguished.

Intraday latency at CPCB is unmeasured; treating day-D trailing hours as complete at the 23:59 IST instant is a declared assumption (the publisher's own daily bulletins show non-participating stations), recorded in the timing block.

Prevalence shift between splits (train 21.15% -> eval 15.66% -> holdout 12.56%): an out-of-distribution as well as temporal test; per-month and per-season tables are shipped in measurements.json beside the pooled figures.

Positives are winter-clustered and station-days within a day are dependent (eval: 19,819 positives over 351 distinct positive days, 509 stations): station-clustered bootstrap intervals accompany every comparison; the distinct-day count is the conservative independent-observation count.

One network, one country, one instrument stream (CPCB CAAQM PM2.5; us_embassy monitors excluded at construction): generalisation beyond India's CAAQM network and the 2019-2024 regime is not established.

The D+1 outcome-observability exclusion (9,368 eval rows unlabelable) could co-move with weather (a monsoon D+1 is both thin and clean); the exclusion is counted per split and per month and never reads the label value, but the conditional structure is a recorded limitation of the selection rule.
required_actions: Before any evaluation: read the evaluation contract in the package quality.json; treat the labeled eval split as development/validation and keep the holdout (145,124 rows / 18,222 positives, sealed) outside evaluated agents' workspaces until a design is frozen

Any evaluated model figure must be quoted beside the pre-registered comparison on the identical eval rows: model 0.9734, station_persistence 0.9689, state_season_climatology 0.8617, majority-class accuracy 0.8434, with the station-clustered intervals from measurements.json
Honest evaluation keeps rows isolated: no cross-row joins (the offset-1 blind join reproduces the label by construction - that is the declared cross-row exposure)

Consumers must keep the GODL-India attribution template for the CPCB measurements and the CC BY 4.0 credits for the XKDR compilation (India Air Quality Database, XKDR Forum; CPCB CAAQM network; US Department of State via AirNow) and the derived-labelling notice in every redistribution
